jobs.description:
As Adv Utilities Professional, you will keep the utility systems in building DF running reliably, so production can run with minimal stops. You will own the daily operation, maintenance and development of these systems, and make sure the building and utilities meet GMP requirements, including in audits and authority inspections. Your work supports a stable, compliant production environment, so medicines can reach people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You combine technical depth with a structured way of working, and you can turn complex technical and regulatory content into clear, usable documentation.

• An engineering degree or a similar technical education. Other academic backgrounds are relevant if you can show strong skills in technical or regulatory documentation.

• Hands-on experience with HVAC, cooling, heating, steam, compressed air or vacuum systems, and with BMS, FMS and CTS systems.

• Experience with documentation, quality, validation or technical support in a GMP-regulated setting.

• Strong written communication: you are precise, correct and professional, and you structure and review documents, so they are easy to use in practice.

• Working knowledge of GMP and ISO 9001 as they apply to daily tasks, and knowledge of CE marking.

• Good collaboration skills in a broad network of stakeholders.

• Experience with structured problem solving such as KATA and A3, or with water systems, calibration, room qualification and validation.

What you’ll do

You will be the process responsible for the operation and maintenance of the utility systems in building DF and the PS Warehouse, and the person colleagues turn to when something needs to be fixed, documented or decided.

• Operate, maintain and optimise utility systems such as HVAC, cooling, heating, steam, compressed air and vacuum, including technical upkeep that keeps unplanned stops to a minimum.

• Make the most of our FMS, CTS and BMS systems for monitoring buildings and room conditions and keep developing how they are used.

• Keep the building and utilities GMP-compliant, from validation and risk assessments to non-conformances, change requests and quality indicators.

• Write, update and review SOPs, service cards, maintenance instructions, machine documentation and validation documents in clear, precise language, and train colleagues in practice.

• Present your own area in audits and authority inspections, and handle urgent utility issues, escalating when needed.

• Drive and support structured problem solving, improvement work and projects such as rebuilds and new purchases, and plan and prioritise your own tasks.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Facility Management team within Global Manufacturing & Supply, where colleagues work across the value chain to keep production running for the people who need our medicines. You will work closely with your team and with technicians, production departments and technical partners in building DF and the PS Warehouse, a site with a large network of stakeholders.

Externally, you will collaborate with facility management providers, the energy supplier in Kalundborg, the Hallas Park landowners’ association and Kalundborg Fire and Rescue Service, as well as other suppliers and Novo Nordisk colleagues. You will agree priorities for the building and shared utilities with production areas, and move between daily operations and cross-organisational coordination. The work is based in Denmark.

What you can expect here

You will work in a complex, GMP-regulated environment where your expertise is valued and your voice is heard. Strong written and technical skills matter here, and the role offers room to build the rest: you will be supported with on-the-job learning, relevant training and close collaboration with experienced colleagues. You are trusted to take ownership, and you will be part of a team that acts with clarity, speed and care for quality.

What we offer

At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary:  For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200.00 to 838,100.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to keep critical utility systems stable, compliant and well documented, apply for the Adv Utilities Professional role by 6 November 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For further information, please contact Carsten Joachim Hansen, Senior manager CJHH@novonordisk.com

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

**Façade Engineer (Buildings and Industry)

**

**Aalborg, Aarhus, Esbjerg, Lyngby, Odense, Vejle

**

**Full-time

**

**Hybrid

**

**Do you want to bring your skills into play on innovative and multidisciplinary projects? Can you contribute to the development of the facade engineering market area? And are you motivated by building relations with colleagues, collaborators, and stakeholders? Then, this is your chance to become part of our skilled facade engineering group and contribute to the buildings of the future!

**

**Contribute to the development of façade engineering

**

The world seeks beautiful and sustainable solutions. To support customers in transforming their aspirations into realities, we are looking for a Façade Engineer to join our team of Façade Specialists. We have a good number of colleagues working alongside our customers on some of Denmark’s most significant projects in construction, such as the Water Culture House on Papirøen and the expansion of Terminal 3 at Copenhagen Airport.

Your main activity will be to participate in project design and supervision within Façade Engineering.

Other key activities will be:

• Identify the need for developing guidelines/procedures/best practices etc.

• Contribute to defining strategies for building relations with collaborators and stakeholders

• Develop external relations with customers

**Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

**

The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

On top of that, you will have:

• A degree in Structural Engineering or related field relevant to façade engineering

• At least 3 years of experience in façade engineering of building structures

• Communication skills in one of the Scandinavian languages and proficiency in English.

**A place to work and so much more

**

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. That is why we say no to fossil-based projects and aspire to have 100% of our revenue come from activities that move our customers towards sustainability.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 8,000 people who bring their knowledge in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

**What we also offer

**

In this role, you will enjoy a rewarding job with significant freedom in a lively, international work environment, including:

• Collaborative opportunities with talented colleagues

• Attractive employment conditions

• Salary in line with industry standards based on your qualifications

• An enriching cultural experience

**Got more questions?

**

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to our Global Talent Acquisition Specialist, Priyanka, at prki@cowi.com.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

**Before you apply

**

We ask that you include your CV along with a cover letter in your application. At the interview, you’ll have the opportunity to share more about your interest in joining COWI.

**Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key.

**

We are committed to creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths. And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting teams and fora. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

Help grow Awaze’s commercial footprint across Germany, Austria and Switzerland by building high-performing travel agency relationships and strategic partnerships that bring our holidays to even more guests.

**Your mission

**As our new Senior Partnership Account Manager, your mission is to grow Awaze’s commercial footprint across the DACH region through two interconnected areas: developing our travel agency channel and building strategic commercial partnerships.

As you’ll be working directly with travel agencies and partners across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, you’ll need to be fluent in German, at native or near-native level, as well as confident communicating professionally in English.

You’ll own and grow relationships with travel agencies across the region, lead agencies through the transition from legacy booking systems to Awaze’s modern platform, and identify new opportunities to expand our network. Alongside this, you’ll develop strategic partnerships from initial prospecting and negotiation through to onboarding and ongoing account development.

Working closely with Marketing, Product, Commercial and leadership teams, you’ll use market insight and performance data to strengthen partner engagement, extend Awaze’s reach and deliver measurable commercial impact.

**What You'll Be Doing

**

• Own and develop relationships with travel agencies across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with a particular focus on chains and networks.

• Lead the end-to-end transition of agencies from legacy booking systems to Awaze’s modern platform, including change management, training and onboarding.

• Identify, develop and onboard new travel agency partners, maintaining a strong pipeline of prospective agencies.

• Proactively identify, pursue, negotiate and close new strategic commercial partnerships across the DACH region.

• Manage the full partnership lifecycle, from initial outreach and commercial negotiation through to onboarding and ongoing account development.

• Monitor agency and partnership performance, using data and commercial metrics to identify opportunities for increased adoption, engagement and growth.

• Collaborate with Marketing, Product and Commercial teams to ensure partners are effectively supported and positioned for success.

• Identify co-marketing and co-branding opportunities that create mutual value and extend Awaze’s reach and brand presence.

• Act as a source of DACH market intelligence, sharing relevant trends, partner feedback and commercial insights with leadership and product teams.

• Travel regularly across the DACH region to build and strengthen relationships with agencies and strategic partners.

**Who We’re Looking For

**You’ll thrive in this role if you’re a natural relationship builder who enjoys turning commercial opportunities into long-term, mutually valuable partnerships. You’re comfortable taking ownership of a varied portfolio, confident working independently and equally at home discussing performance data, negotiating a new partnership or helping an established agency embrace a new way of working.

Fluent German, at native or near-native level, is an essential requirement for this role. You’ll use German regularly to build trusted relationships and communicate effectively with travel agencies and strategic partners across the DACH region.

**We’re Looking For Someone Who Brings

**

• Several years of experience in account management, partnerships or business development, ideally within travel, hospitality or a related sector.

• A demonstrable track record of growing accounts and closing partnerships that deliver measurable commercial outcomes.

• Fluent German, at native or near-native level, alongside strong professional English, both written and spoken.

• Strong relationship-building, communication and presentation skills, with the credibility to engage agency owners, commercial partners and senior stakeholders.

• Strong analytical capabilities and confidence using performance data and commercial metrics to inform decisions and identify opportunities.

• An understanding of brand and marketing principles and the ability to represent Awaze consistently with external partners.

• A self-motivated and structured approach, with the ability to independently manage a large and varied account portfolio.

• Willingness and ability to travel regularly across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, as well as other locations when required.

• Bonus points if you have experience within the DACH travel agency landscape, legacy travel booking systems or digital platform transitions, or have worked within or alongside a major European travel group.

• An established network across DACH travel agencies or hospitality chains, or experience with GDS tools and partnership management platforms, would also be an advantage.

**How You'll Make An Impact

**

• Successfully transition and onboard travel agencies onto Awaze’s modern platform, driving strong adoption and engagement.

• Grow the number, quality and performance of active travel agency relationships across the DACH region.

• Build and maintain a healthy pipeline of prospective agencies and strategic partners, progressing opportunities through to successful commercial agreements.

• Strengthen retention, satisfaction and commercial performance across your agency and partnership portfolio.

• Turn performance data into clear insights and recommendations that help both our partners and internal teams make better commercial decisions.

• Work across Marketing, Product and Commercial teams to unlock partner support, co-marketing opportunities and additional commercial value.

• Bring relevant DACH market trends, partner feedback and insights into Awaze to help inform product and business decisions.

• Champion Awaze’s brands and standards across every agency and partner interaction.

**Why you’ll want to work at Awaze

**We offer a versatile position in a strong professional and social environment - one you’ll have the opportunity to influence and help shape. You’ll be part of an international company that invests in the future, and join a dynamic, fast-paced department with skilled and committed colleagues who support each other.

We’re a People-first Business - And We Know That Our Success Starts With Our Teams. Here’s a Glimpse Of What You’ll Enjoy

• Generous discounts on holidays across our brands

• Flexible hybrid working – with the autonomy to work how you work best

• Real opportunities to grow, learn and shape your role as well as careers progression vertically or horizontally, cross countries and responsibilities.

**About Awaze

**Our mission is clear - to create amazing holidays with Europe’s widest choice of holiday homes.

With more than 110,000 properties across Europe, we are the largest managed vacation rentals business in the region. Our ambition is not only to be the biggest, but the best provider of holiday homes in Europe.

As travel continues to evolve, we are focused on what comes next. We will keep strengthening our relationships with guests and homeowners, continuously improving the way we work, and delivering strong performance. By making things simpler and smarter, we are building a business that is ready for what’s next - powered by proud, passionate and inclusive people.

**Worth knowing

**

• This role can be based remotely in Germany or from our Virum office in Denmark.

• Regular travel across Germany, Austria and Switzerland will be an important part of the role, with travel to other locations when required.

**What’s next?

**If this sounds like the right next step for you, hit “Apply” and follow the instructions to submit your application. We tailor our recruitment process to each role to give both you and our hiring teams the best possible chance to assess whether this could be the start of a successful collaboration. You’ll hear from us shortly after we’ve reviewed your application.

We’re committed to running an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. All applicants will receive equal consideration for employment, and if you have any specific requirements or adjustments needed for the interview, just let us know when you accept your invitation - we’re happy to accommodate.

Do you enjoy handling all kinds of user’s questions related to computers? Are you passionate about IT support? If both answers are yes, we can offer you a challenging position, great colleagues and the opportunity to combine your education with hand-on experience in a global company.

Your main responsibilities

We offer

• A versatile and challenging job with focus on developing and expanding your skills

Application / next step

DHI are the first people you should call when you have a tough challenge to solve in a water environment – be it a river, a reservoir, an ocean, a coastline, within a city or a factory.

Our knowledge of water environments is second-to-none. It represents 50 years of dedicated research and real-life experience from more than 140 countries. We strive to make this knowledge globally accessible to clients and partners by channelling it through our local teams and unique software.

Our world is water. So whether you need to save water, share it fairly, improve its quality, quantify its impact or manage its flow, we can help. Our knowledge, combined with our team's expertise and the power of our technology, holds the key to unlocking the right solution.

For more information please visit www.dhigroup.com

Join us in this role where you’ll act as the accounting lead on some of the world’s largest and most complex renewable energy transactions. Your IFRS expertise will help shape transaction structures and inform key investment decisions. You’ll assess the accounting implications of complex M&A transactions, advise on proposed structures, and translate your conclusions into clear insights that support commercial decisions.

**Welcome to IC Projects & IFRS

**You’ll be part of IC Projects & IFRS where you will act as the accounting lead on M&A transactions including acquisitions, divestments, farm-downs, joint ventures, and strategic partnerships. You’ll join a highly specialised team of eight accounting professionals and work closely with our Partnerships and M&A organisation, external advisers, auditors, and a team of around 40 M&A professionals who originate and execute transactions across Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific. In this role, you’ll support complex international transactions and help ensure high-quality accounting decisions across the Group.

As a team, we share knowledge, explore complex accounting questions together, and support one another in delivering high-quality advice. We value different perspectives, open dialogue, flexibility, and a healthy work-life balance.

**You’ll play an important role in:

**

• acting as the IFRS accounting lead on acquisitions, divestments, farm-downs, joint ventures, structured financing arrangements, and strategic partnerships

• assessing accounting implications early in the transaction process and advising on proposed deal and investment structures

• preparing clear IFRS accounting assessments and technical memos that support commercial and management decisions

• reviewing draft contracts, term sheets, bid materials, and other transaction documentation from an accounting perspective

• participating in meetings with investors, external advisers, auditors, and internal stakeholders on transaction-related accounting matters

• contributing to wider Group Finance activities, including financial reporting, accounting policy development, and strategic accounting projects.

**To succeed in the role, you:

**

• bring deep IFRS expertise gained through technical accounting, IFRS advisory or a similar specialist environment

• have experience advising on the IFRS implications of M&A transactions within a listed company, international group, professional services firm, or a comparable organisation

• can translate complex accounting matters into clear, practical conclusions for management, commercial colleagues, and other non-accounting stakeholders

• build strong working relationships and communicate confidently across finance, Partnerships & M&A, management, external advisers, and auditors

• approach complex assignments analytically and systematically, take ownership of your work, and remain adaptable to changing transaction priorities

• hold a master’s degree in accounting, auditing, or a related discipline.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

**Shape the future with us

**Send your application to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com.

Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country. We don't take applications or inquiries from external recruiters or agencies into account for this position.

**Position salary range:

**For this position, the expected base pay range is kr64,720.00- kr116,496.00 for the advertised location. The offered base salary will be determined within this range based on relevant skills, experience, and expected role fulfilment within the stated pay range to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Our benefits package:

**For this position, employees who meet eligibility requirements have access to: employer‑paid pension (11% contribution), full insurance coverage (accident, life, critical illness, and health insurance); five weeks of paid holiday plus 10 additional paid days off per holiday year; a 3% holiday allowance; access to Ørsted Life & Fitness Vitality including fitness classes, physiotherapy, massage, and wellbeing programmes; a multimedia package (mobile phone, PC, internet); staff club membership with sport and cultural activities; and access to the company canteen (monthly lunch scheme or daily tickets).

**Pre-employment background check:

**Certain positions may require a background check as part of the hiring process. If applicable, you will be informed during the recruitment process. Background checks are conducted by an external provider in accordance with local legal requirements.

**Do you want to be at the forefront of protecting our society against cyber threats? We are looking for a Key account manager to our Commercial organization.

**About Truesec – A Leading Cybersecurity Company

**Since 2005, Truesec has been a native cybersecurity company, driven by one single purpose: Creating safety and sustainability in a digital world by preventing cyber breach and minimizing impact.

Over the years, we’ve earned the trust of organizations worldwide and gained a strong reputation internationally. Our team consists of dedicated specialists covering the entire spectrum of cybersecurity – with capabilities in Predict, Prevent, Protect, Respond, and Recover.

Today, we employ around 400 employees – and as cybercrime grows, we need to grow. To support that goal, we are now looking for a Key Account Manager who wants to make a difference.

**The Role

**At Truesec Denmark, we're on the lookout for an experienced Key Account Manager to drive our continued growth by winning new business and nurturing strong relationships with our great customers. As one of the primary points of contact, you will ensure our customers remain satisfied while we drive our business forward with high professionalism. You will cover customers in all of Denmark however the majority of your key accounts will be in Jutland. You will also:

• Create new business: Take the initiative and discover new opportunities to expand our customer portfolio. You will have freedom to set goals and initiatives that makes the Danish team perform even better than today.

• Build & retain relationships: Develop and maintain strong bonds with our customers, ensuring their needs are consistently met.

• Understand customer & market needs: Gain deep insights into our customers’ business goals and cybersecurity requirements in general.

• Drive growth: Identify chances to expand existing partnerships through upselling and cross-selling.

• Collaborate internally: Work closely with our teams to ensure we deliver solutions that exceed customer expectations.

• Monitor and report: Keep an eye on customer satisfaction, account performance, and market trends, and share your insights with the team.

• Stay informed: Keep up with the latest industry trends, emerging threats, and competitive developments to always offer the best advice.

**Your Potential Background

**To succeed in this role, we believe that you

• Bring extensive experience from the cybersecurity industry.

• Have a proven success as a Key Account Manager or in a similar client-facing role, ideally within the cybersecurity sector.

• Demonstrate exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, fostering strong connections with clients and stakeholders.

• Possess a proactive, results-oriented attitude and thrives in dynamic, fast-paced environments.

• Excel in organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities simultaneously.

• Have a track record of building and maintaining long-term, trusted client relationships.

• Tackles challenges with a solution-driven mindset and remains composed under pressure.

• Are proficient in CRM tools (preferably Hubspot) and skilled in using the Microsoft Office Suite.

• Exhibit business-level fluency in reading, writing, and speaking both Danish and English.

Due to the sensitivity in our assignments, we require Danish or Swedish citizenship or citizenship in an EU country.

**Join Our Mission Toward a Safe Digital Future

**If you truly want to make a difference and make our world a little bit safer, this is the place for you. At Truesec, you'll get to be at the forefront of fighting cybercrime instead of reading about it in the news. This is your chance to be part of an exciting journey in a leading cybersecurity company - and learn from some of the best in their field.

So, are you ready to team up with the most dedicated team of experts and be part of a meaningful mission? Then we are excited to get to know you!

About Photoncycle

Solar panels make plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that for households. We store energy from the summer sun, so that the it can be used all winter. When there’s excess energy, we sell the surplus to the grid, where it helps balance supply and demand. Households pay a fixed monthly fee; we build, install and operate the system.

Our mission is to accelerate the transition to a more renewable, balanced, and secure energy system. Photoncycle systems enable households to use homegrown energy year-round for electricity, heat, and hot water, while also helping the grid balance production and consumption peaks. This enables the transition away from fossil-based energy.

Our customers are central to that mission. Every home we power is proof that energy independence is possible, and the stories of those homeowners are one of our strongest tools for reaching the next ones.

We are a team of 25 employees across offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026, we raised a €15 million Series A backed by NordicNinja, Voima Ventures, Lifeline Ventures, Eviny Ventures, Luminar Ventures and Momentum. We're now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, with the first phase of our production facility coming online in 2027.

The Role

We are looking for a Storyteller to own content creation and community management for our customers. Your main goal is to engage our customers with compelling, on-brand content, and to make Photoncycle something people want to follow, talk about and belong to.

You will shape how Photoncycle shows up on all communications channels, in both Danish and English. That means developing content concepts for social media, writing for our different platforms, and working with external photographers, videographers and agencies to bring ideas to life. You will also be the voice of our brand in our community channels, and you will create moments that bring customers, their neighbours, and future customers together.

Much of this is still unbuilt. Our Danish rollout is in its early phase, so you will spend a considerable amount of time testing formats, trying new ideas, and learning what resonates. We value creativity, curiosity, a structured way of working, and the ability to connect what you create to what the company and the customer actually need, not just the next post in the calendar.

You don't need to be an energy expert from day one. We will support you in learning about the energy markets, and there are experts to help you anytime.

You will join the the small Danish team that is building the market from the ground up, while also contributing to the global storytelling of Photoncycle. You will work closely with operations, product and our marketing colleagues in Oslo to turn a deep-tech product into stories people understand and remember.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and own the content strategy and content calendar across our channels, in Danish and English, tied to clear goals for engagement, awareness and customer loyalty.

• Shape the Photoncycle brand story, from our mission to the everyday lives of the homeowners who live with our system.

• Develop content concepts and recurring formats for social media that fit how each platform works.

• Write copy for our different platforms, including social media, newsletters, website, customer communication, and customer stories.

• Brief and manage external partners (photographers, videographers, agencies and freelancers) from concept to final delivery.

• Manage our customer community: engage, respond, moderate, spark conversations, and share customer insights with sales, service and product.

• Track performance, report on engagement and reach, and use the data to improve what we do.

What We're Looking For

Must-have experience

• Experience with concept development, content strategy and creation, brand storytelling or social media, in-house or at an agency.

• Excellent written Danish and strong written English.

• A solid understanding of the logic of social media platforms: algorithms, formats, and what drives reach and engagement.

• Strong project management skills: able to run several projects in parallel and deliver on time.

• Ability to explain complex or technical topics in plain, human language.

• Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where the right answer isn't known yet.

Nice-to-have

• Experience working with external partners to produce content, such as video and images.

• Experience with community management or building online and offline communities.

• Background in energy, climate tech, home improvement, or other considered consumer purchases.

• Hands-on skills in short-form video, photo editing or design tools, for example CapCut, Adobe or Canva.

• Experience with social analytics, newsletter tools, CRM, or paid social.

We welcome applicants across experience levels, from motivated early-career storytellers to more senior profiles. If you bring a strong creative sense and genuine curiosity for this domain, we encourage you to apply even if you do not match every item above exactly.

What Success Looks Like

• Photoncycle has a recognisable, consistent brand voice that customers and prospects engage with.

• Our customers feel part of a community and share their experience with neighbours, friends and online.

• Content formats, partners and processes are in place so we can produce high-quality content at a steady pace, and scale it to new markets.

• The team makes better marketing and customer decisions by bringing engagement data and customer insight into the discussion, and you'll be part of making that happen.

What We Offer

• The opportunity to shape the voice of a high-impact climate technology company in one of its first markets.

• A central role in connecting Photoncycle's customers, product and brand.

• A collaborative, mission-driven culture with significant ownership.

• An office in the heart of Copenhagen at BLOXhub with lunch benefits and unlimited coffee.

Photoncycle is committed to building an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and make hiring decisions based on skills, experience, and potential.

About Flatpay

As a Data Engineer in the Marketing team at Flatpay, you’ll collaborate closely with marketers, BI engineers, and analysts to turn business needs into scalable data solutions. You’ll help build and evolve event-driven ETL/ELT pipelines for lead intake, routing, and enrichment, as well as the data platform that powers marketing insights.

What you'll do

• 
Design, build, and operate lead flow pipelines, including monitoring and alerting to ensure reliability

• 
Contribute to the development of internal tools and frameworks for marketing data ingestion and transformation

• 
Enable self-service analytics by structuring clean, well-documented datasets for dashboards and reporting tools

• 
Partner with marketing analysts and stakeholders to translate business needs into robust data solutions

• 
Build and maintain data models that support campaign performance tracking, attribution, and customer segmentation

Who you are

You are a pragmatic and detail-oriented problem solver who enjoys building data systems that directly impact business growth. You’re comfortable working cross-functionally with marketers, analysts, and engineers, and you can communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

Must-haves

• 
0–3 years of experience as a Data Engineer or similar role

• 
Solid understanding of ETL/ELT design and data modeling principles

• 
Strong Python and SQL skills in production environments

• 
Exposure to cloud infrastructure (Azure, AWS, or GCP)

• 
Strong attention to data quality and consistency

Nice-to-haves

• 
Experience with marketing data and attribution models

• 
Experience with CI/CD workflows, version control (e.g., Git), and testing best practices

• 
Familiarity with data orchestration tools (e.g., Airflow, Prefect, Azure Data Factory)

jobs.occupation: Postdoc Position: Endocrine Disruption in Fish with Focus on Histopathological Endpoint Development
jobs.description:
We invite applicants for a 3½-years Postdoctoral research position in Environmental Toxicology with a focus on histopathological and behavioral endpoints development in fish. The position is funded by the EU Partnership for Risk Assessment of Chemicals (PARC), the Danish EPA and University of Southern Denmark (SDU). The project will be carried out in the Ecotoxicology group at the Department of Biology, SDU. 

Qualifications: 
The successful candidate must hold a PhD degree in Environmental Toxicology. A strong background in chemical risk and hazard assessment and regulatory toxicology is highly appreciated. This includes knowledge of EU chemicals legislation and regulatory frameworks such as REACH, OECD test guidelines, AOP development, and/or pesticide and biocide risk assessment. Furthermore, the following experiences and skills are required: 

• 
Strong proficiency in English, both written and verbal. 

• 
Experience in teaching and supervision at the university level, including lectures, student examinations, and supervision of MSc students. 

• 
Hands-on experience in assessing endocrine disruption properties of chemicals using the Zebrafish (Danio rerio) model.  

• 
Strong documented knowledge of one or more endocrine pathways relevant to EU regulatory assessments (EATS modalities). 

• 
Extensive experience with OECD fish test protocols such as OECD TG 236 and OECD TG 210. 

• 
Documented experience in histopathology techniques, including tissue preparation, microtome sectioning, cryosectioning, H&E staining, microscopy, and image analysis. 

• 
Experience in behavioral assessment in zebrafish eleutheroembryos, e.g., using EthoVision XT or equivalent tracking and analysis software. 

The following qualifications are considered advantageous: 

• 
Experience with molecular biology techniques, including gene expression analysis (e.g., qPCR, transcriptomics). 

• 
Experience with immunohistochemistry and related imaging techniques. 

This position is particularly suited for a candidate with strong interest in bridging experimental ecotoxicology and regulatory chemical risk- and hazard assessment. 

Application deadline: 13. November 2026 at 23:59 hours local Danish time. 
Please see the full call, including how to apply, on www.sdu.dk

jobs.occupation: Chief Flight Instructor at GreyBird Pilot Academy - HQ located at Aarhus Airport, DK –  Ready to shape the future of pilot training? ✈️
jobs.description:
GreyBird Pilot Academy is more than a flight school. We are a fast-growing international business in an industry that never stands still – training the next generation of commercial pilots.

Since starting out in Aarhus in 2013, we have grown to seven bases across Europe – from Dublin in the west to Helsinki in the east. Our students fly under the Spanish sun and across European airspace. Today, more than 200 students are training to become commercial pilots with us, supported by over 40 flight instructors and a fleet of 12 Tecnam aircraft, with 13 more on the way.

This is where ambition becomes reality – where safety, people, technology, operations and training must all come together before the wheels leave the runway.

You have an aviation background and have instructed from the cockpit yourself. With us, you will join a highly skilled team with short decision-making lines and plenty of room to shape our development. We turn the dream of flying into a career – and you can help make that journey even better.

The role

The Chief Flight Instructor (CFI) is part of our ATO Core Team and holds overall responsibility for quality, standardisation and compliance in the flight and simulator training delivered by our flight instructors.

You are appointed by the Accountable Manager and report directly to the Head of Training, with whom you work closely to ensure consistent, high-quality training. The Head of Training may delegate tasks and authority to you within your area of responsibility.

Your key responsibilities include:

• 
Standardisation, supervision and training planning for the entire instructor team

• 
Developing and enforcing standard operating procedures for flight training

• 
Ensuring that all instructors hold valid licences, certificates and competencies

• 
Recruiting new instructors as well as guiding, mentoring and providing recurrent training for the existing team

• 
Assessing new bases as we expand into new countries

• 
Updating training materials and operations manuals on our in-house platform, SmartBird

• 
Taking part in ATO and management meetings, where you help set the direction for training

What we offer:

• 
Real decision-making authority over training quality and standards in a growing international organisation

• 
A direct reporting line to the Head of Training and close ties to management

• 
An established ATO with a clear, EASA-approved framework for the role

• 
Access to a modern and growing fleet

• 
An international working environment with colleagues and instructors from several countries

Requirements

The Chief Flight Instructor is a nominated post under EASA Part-ORA (ORA.ATO.210). In line with the regulation, the CFI must hold the highest pilot licence and at least one instructor certificate relevant to the courses the school offers. As GreyBird offers ATPL theory, several aircraft types and type rating-related training, we are looking for:

• 
CPL(A) or ATPL(A)

• 
Instructor certificate: FI(A)

• 
Additional instructor certificates such as CRI(A) and IRI(A) are considered an advantage

• 
A minimum of 1,000 hours as PIC, including at least 500 hours of instructional flying (industry practice is typically 1,500+ hours, and more experience counts in your favour)

• 
Ideally, you also have experience leading, standardising or developing other instructors

• 
Fluent English, spoken and written

How to apply

Ready to set the course for a role where you shape the standards for the next generation of pilots? Send us your application today – we look forward to hearing from you.

About Lightbooth

Lightbooth sells photobooths and selfie machines with an integrated CRM and marketing system, designed for restaurants, nightlife venues, entertainment and experience venues.

We’re a fast-growing company, with Scandinavia, the UK and Spain currently our largest markets. Your focus will be on the UK, Ireland and the Nordics, with the freedom to pursue customers throughout Europe.

Your role

You’ll find potential customers, connect with decision-makers and show them how Lightbooth can add value to their business. You’ll take ownership of the sales process, from first contact to closing the deal.

Your responsibilities will include:

• 
Identifying and reaching out to potential customers.

• 
Presenting our photobooths and CRM and marketing system.

• 
Following up on leads and turning conversations into agreements.

• 
Building customer relationships across European markets.

There may be opportunities to travel for customer visits, giving you the chance to build a strong international network across the nightlife, hospitality and entertainment industries.

What you bring

You enjoy meeting new people, understand what makes a business tick and know how to turn interest into action. You’re ambitious, optimistic and persistent enough to keep a conversation moving when a deal takes time.

We’re looking for someone who:

• 
Is a confident communicator and fluent in English.

• 
Has commercial instincts and is motivated by results.

• 
Takes initiative and works independently.

• 
Follows through and takes ownership of their sales activities.

• 
Is eager to learn and develop their sales skills.

An interest in nightlife is a big plus, especially if you understand the environment our customers work in. Additional major European languages are also an advantage, but aren’t required.

What we offer

• 
Up to 15 hours per week – a good fit alongside your studies.

• 
Base pay and an attractive commission scheme, rewarding the results you deliver.

• 
An office in central Copenhagen, with flexibility in how you organise your work and achieve your goals.

• 
Hands-on international sales experience in a fast-growing company.

• 
Opportunities for customer visits across Europe and to build a valuable international network.

Interested? Let’s talk.

Send your CV and a few lines about yourself to job@lightbooth.dk. Tell us what interests you about the role and which languages you speak.

Good decisions start with good data. But good data does not just happen. At NORDEN, data comes from many places and is used across our business to understand markets, automate processes and make better decisions. Your job is to make sure that data is actually ready to be used.

As our new Data Engineer, you will build the pipelines and datasets that move data through our organisation and turn raw information into something people can trust and work with.

You will not be sitting far away from the business maintaining pipelines no one really talks about. You will work closely with digital and commercial colleagues, understand what they need and build the data foundation that helps them solve real problems.

And while shipping knowledge is something you will pick up along the way, curiosity about data and how to make it useful is something we hope you bring from day one.

Why this role?

Because there is a lot to build, improve and figure out.

You will join nine colleagues in our Data Engineering team in Copenhagen, working with large and varied datasets using PySpark, SQL, Azure DevOps and Microsoft Fabric. And our team is growing beyond Copenhagen. We are setting up a Data Engineering team in Singapore, starting with two colleagues, giving you an even broader team to work and share ideas with.

Some days will be about building something new. Others will be about improving what already exists, finding a smarter way to structure data or figuring out why something is not working quite as expected.

What connects it all is the purpose behind it: making data easier to trust, access and use across NORDEN.

You already know your way around data engineering. Now you are looking for a role where you can have more of a say in how things are built, not just build what has already been decided.

You will manage your solutions, contribute to technical decisions and collaborate closely with the business to understand what our data needs to do.

What you will be doing

You will work across the journey from raw data to reliable datasets that colleagues and systems across NORDEN can actually use.

You will:

• Build and maintain scalable data pipelines.

• Bring internal and external data together and turn it into trusted datasets.

• Transform raw data into useful features and insights.

• Improve how we capture, validate and enrich data.

• Build solutions that are reliable today without making life difficult for whoever needs to work with them tomorrow.

• Work with digital and commercial colleagues to understand what they need from our data and translate that into technical solutions.

What you bring

You know that good data solutions are not only about getting things to work, but about making them reliable, scalable and useful to others.

Besides this you likely have:

• Around 5 years of practical experience in data engineering or a similar role.

• A degree within data, IT, engineering or another analytical field.

• Eligibility to work in Denmark.

• Solid experience with Lakehouse architecture, for example in Microsoft Fabric or Azure Databricks.

• Experience designing and building data pipelines and working with how data is structured, transformed and made available to others.

• Experience contributing to technical decisions around data architecture and how data should be structured and used.

• The confidence to be responsible for your solutions, while still enjoying sparring with and learning from others.

• Good English communication skills, both written and spoken.

Our company

We are a global provider of ocean-based freight services for bulk and project cargo of all sizes. We integrate freight solutions with port logistics, helping our customers optimise and decarbonise supply chains. We provide tailored solutions built on flexibility, reliability, and intelligence.

Our agile business model ensures stability by continuously adapting our fleet to market developments and customer needs.

Founded in 1871, NORDEN is one of Denmark’s oldest internationally operating shipping companies. Incorporated in Denmark, we are listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen as part of the OMX Nordic Large Cap index.

With offices across 6 continents, we are a truly integrated part of global trade.

You know shipping. Now you can use that knowledge in a completely different way.

At NORDEN, our core business applications sit right at the heart of how our commercial teams work. But getting the most out of them is not only about the technology. It is about understanding how shipping actually works, how people use the systems every day and where things could work better.

As our new Business Application Manager, you will bring your shipping experience into that space.

You will work with colleagues across NORDEN to improve how we use our core business applications, optimise the processes around them and help turn business needs into better ways of working.

You do not need to come from IT or have worked as a Business Application Manager before. You understand shipping, likely from operations, control/finance or laytime and are curious about how systems and technology can make the business work better.

Why this role?

Because you get to use your shipping knowledge from a completely new angle.

You will join our Business Applications team of six colleagues across Copenhagen, Cyprus and Singapore, working closely with colleagues from the business as well as Digital Services and Solutions.

Your primary focus will be IMOS, but your work will also take you into applications such as SEDNA, PortLog, Shipfix and other tools used across NORDEN.

Some days you might be looking at how a process could work better in IMOS. Others you could be helping colleagues get more out of an application, supporting a new implementation or working with our commercial AI assistant tools.

What connects it all is understanding how people work today and finding ways for our systems and processes to support them better.

Your base will be our office in Hellerup, with occasional travel to other NORDEN offices.

What you will be doing

You will work where shipping, people, processes and technology meet.

You will:

• Analyse how our business applications and surrounding processes are used and identify opportunities to improve them.

• Participate in and lead projects implementing new applications, processes and integrations.

• Train and support colleagues in getting the most out of our applications.

• Work with teams across NORDEN to create better alignment between processes and systems.

• Support and develop the use of our commercial AI assistant tools.

• Work primarily with IMOS while also getting involved with SEDNA, PortLog, Shipfix and other business applications.

What you bring

You do not need to be an IT specialist. What matters most is your understanding of shipping and how these applications are used in practice. You may have used them as an end user up to now, and that experience could be exactly what makes you well suited for this role.

Besides this you likely:

• Have experience from shipping, from operations, control/finance or laytime.

• Have worked with shipping business applications and are familiar with IMOS.

• Are curious about technology, AI and digitalisation and how they can improve the way a business operates.

You are curious about how people work and what could make their day-to-day easier. You listen, ask questions and connect the dots between people, processes and systems, turning what you learn into practical improvements.
